_notes: Industry salary benchmarks sourced from ABS Employee Earnings, Hours and Leave Survey (EEH) 2023-24 and ABS Labour Force Survey. Weekly median earnings multiplied by 52. Quintile distributions are estimated from the ABS earnings percentile data where available; otherwise interpolated from known P25/P50/P75 values assuming a lognormal distribution. All figures are approximate.
_quintile_note: salary_quintiles = [Q1_mean, Q2_mean, Q3_mean(≈median), Q4_mean, Q5_mean]. Each quintile represents 20% of employees. Weighting each at 0.20 gives an unbiased estimate of E[tax(salary)] rather than tax(E[salary]), correcting for the convexity of progressive tax brackets (Jensen's inequality).
_oecd_tax_wedge_note: For context: Australia's OECD average tax wedge on labour (employee + employer taxes / gross labour cost) is approximately 28-30% for an average wage worker, compared to OECD average of ~35%.

Mining.quintile_source: ABS EEH 2023-24 Cat. 6306.0, estimated quintile midpoints from P25/P50/P75 data
Mining.notes: Highest-paid industry in Australia. Wide distribution: mine operators, drivers and trades at lower quintiles; engineers, managers and executives at upper quintiles. FIFO loadings push median up significantly.

Finance and Insurance Services.notes: Very wide salary distribution. Bank tellers and customer service in Q1-Q2; analysts, advisers in Q3; senior bankers, fund managers in Q4-Q5. Large Q5 reflects executive remuneration especially at major banks and Macquarie.

Electricity, Gas, Water and Waste Servic.notes: Relatively compressed distribution compared to finance. High union coverage in utility workers; significant technical and engineering workforce.

Construction.notes: Includes many subcontractors and owner-operators (not captured in wage data). Wide range from labourers to project managers and directors.

Professional, Scientific and Technical S.notes: Covers legal, accounting, engineering, IT consulting and scientific research. Graduate-heavy workforce with significant upper-tail dispersion from partners and principals.

Information Media and Telecommunications.notes: Tech companies (software, fintech) at higher quintiles; media, content and customer service roles at lower quintiles. Significant equity compensation at listed tech firms not captured in wage data.

Health Care and Social Assistance.notes: Large workforce, moderate salary dispersion. Aged care and disability support workers at Q1; nurses, allied health at Q2-Q3; specialists and radiologists at Q4-Q5. Many part-time workers inflate employee count relative to FTE.

Education and Training.notes: Relatively compressed distribution due to public sector award rates. Many casual and part-time academics at lower quintiles; full professors and principals at upper end.

Transport, Postal and Warehousing.notes: Covers truck drivers, warehouse workers, airline staff, postal workers and logistics management. Qantas aviation crews and Australia Post include significant shift and penalty loadings.

Wholesale Trade.notes: Warehouse and sales roles at lower quintiles; account managers and category buyers at mid; directors and owners at upper quintiles.

Retail Trade.notes: Large casual and part-time workforce significantly depresses the median. Full-time store managers and buyers sit at Q3-Q4. Q1 represents many part-time retail assistants. Woolworths and Coles employ at scale in this range.

Accommodation and Food Services.notes: Lowest-paid industry. Large proportion of casual, part-time and junior workers. Reflects seasonal tourism employment. Many workers at or near minimum wage.

Arts and Recreation Services.notes: Wide variation: casual venue staff at lower quintiles; performers, technicians and facility managers in mid range; senior managers and executives at top.

Other Services.notes: Catch-all category including repair services, personal care, funeral services, religious organisations.
